activities.title: Burning magnesium ribbon
activities.summary: Clean Mg ribbon with sandpaper; burn in air; collect white magnesium oxide ash.

activities.title: Lead nitrate and potassium iodide
activities.summary: Mix Pb(NO₃)₂ and KI solutions; observe yellow precipitate of lead iodide.

activities.title: Zinc with dilute acid
activities.summary: Add dilute HCl or H₂SO₄ to zinc granules; test hydrogen gas with burning splint.

activities.title: Quick lime with water
activities.summary: Add water to calcium oxide; feel temperature rise as slaked lime forms.

activities.title: Heating ferrous sulphate
activities.summary: Heat green FeSO₄·7H₂O crystals; observe colour change and SO₂/SO₃ gases.

activities.title: Heating lead nitrate
activities.summary: Heat lead nitrate powder; observe brown NO₂ fumes and residue.

activities.title: Electrolysis of water
activities.summary: Pass current through acidified water; collect H₂ and O₂ in inverted tubes.

activities.title: Silver chloride in sunlight
activities.summary: Expose white AgCl to sunlight; it turns grey as silver and chlorine form.

activities.title: Iron nails in copper sulphate
activities.summary: Immerse iron in CuSO₄; blue colour fades and brown copper deposits on iron.

activities.title: Barium chloride and sodium sulphate
activities.summary: Mix solutions; white BaSO₄ precipitate forms.

activities.title: Heating copper powder
activities.summary: Heat copper in air; black CuO forms; reduction with hydrogen gives copper back.

exercise_mcqs.question:
Which of the statements about the reaction below are incorrect?
2PbO(s) + C(s) → 2Pb(s) + CO₂(g)
(a) Lead is getting reduced.
(b) Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised.
(c) Carbon is getting oxidised.
(d) Lead oxide is getting reduced.
exercise_mcqs.explanation: PbO loses oxygen (reduced); C gains oxygen (oxidised to CO₂). Statements (a) and (b) are incorrect.

exercise_mcqs.question:
Fe₂O₃ + 2Al → Al₂O₃ + 2Fe
The above reaction is an example of a
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Aluminium displaces iron from iron(III) oxide — a displacement (thermit-type) reaction.

exercise_mcqs.question: What happens when dilute hydrochloric acid is added to iron filings? Tick the correct answer.
options: Hydrogen gas and iron chloride are produced.
Chlorine gas and iron hydroxide are produced.
Iron salt and water are produced.
exercise_mcqs.explanation: Fe + 2HCl → FeCl₂ + H₂ — hydrogen gas evolves and iron(II) chloride forms.

intext_samples.question: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
options: To increase its weight before burning
To remove the oxide layer so it burns readily
To make it shine for observation only
To convert it to magnesium oxide first
intext_samples.explanation: Magnesium ribbon is cleaned with sandpaper to remove the oxide coating that would otherwise slow reaction with oxygen.

intext_samples.question: Is Mg + O₂ → MgO a balanced chemical equation?
options: Yes, atoms are equal on both sides
No, oxygen atoms are not equal
No, magnesium atoms are not equal
It is a physical change equation
intext_samples.explanation: Left side has 2 O atoms in O₂ but only 1 O in MgO — the equation is unbalanced until written as 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.

intext_samples.question: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ releases heat. This reaction is best described as
intext_samples.explanation: Calcium oxide and water combine to form a single product (slaked lime) with release of heat — exothermic combination.

intext_samples.question: When an iron nail is dipped in blue copper sulphate solution, the solution turns pale green because
options: Fe²⁺ ions replace Cu²⁺ in solution
intext_samples.explanation: Fe displaces Cu from CuSO₄ forming FeSO₄ (pale green); copper metal deposits on the nail.

intext_samples.question: In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is reduced?
intext_samples.explanation: CuO loses oxygen and is reduced to Cu; H₂ is oxidised to H₂O.
